  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.

2)                 Apply your understanding of requirements engineering to identify and describe various requirements (5)  
  gathering techniques commonly used by analysts, explaining how each technique is implemented in

A)   practice.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)   Illustrate the Rapid Application Development (RAD) life cycle model and demonstrate how it            (5)  
  enables faster software development while effectively handling user change requests.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)        How can the concept of functional independence be described in the context of software design?        (5)  
  Discuss how design principles such as cohesion and coupling contribute to achieving functional  
  A)   independence, and explain the advantages this provides in developing reliable and maintainable  
  software  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)   Explain the concept of cohesion in software design. Using suitable examples, describe the following (5)  
  types of cohesion:  
  
  1. Logical cohesion  
  2. Procedural cohesion  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)        An Insurance Management System assists a company in handling claim requests efficiently.              (5)  
  The system performs the following key operations:  
  A)  
  1. Policyholder Registration  
  2. Claim Submission  
  3. Claim Verification  
  4. Decision on Approval or Rejection  
  5. Claim Status Update and Customer Notification  
  
  Using the principles of UML Communication Modelling, illustrate the interactions among major  
  entities such as Customer, Claim Handler, Verification Unit, Database, and Notification Module  
  using sequence diagram.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)   A Library Management System is designed to automate various library operations such as member (5)  
  registration, book issuance, returns, fine calculation, and inventory updates. The major functions of  
  the system include: registering members, searching and issuing books, returning books, calculating  
  fines for late submissions, and updating the book inventory. Using the concepts of UML Component  
  Diagrams, demonstrate how these operations can be organized into modular software components.  
  Identify and illustrate the interaction among key components such as the User Interface, Book  
  Database, Transaction Manager, Fine Calculator, and Report Generator.Draw a schematic  
  Component Diagram showing the interfaces, dependencies, and relationships among these  
  components to represent the functional architecture of the system.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5)        Design a black-box test suite for a function that takes the name of a book as input and searches a (5)  
  file containing the names of the books available in the Library and displays the details of the book if  
  A)   the book is available in the library otherwise displays the message "book not available.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)   Apply your understanding of integration testing to illustrate how stubs and drivers are used in the   (5)

  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"
